union.summary: Fix breaks legitimate single-dash setext H2 headings (`Heading\n-`), a behavior change the issue never asked for
union.evidence:
`const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1;` unconditionally rejects ANY single-dash setext underline, regardless of whether the line is inside a list or is a plain top-level paragraph. Combined with `wrappedList` returning `true` in silent mode for any empty bullet line while `state.parentType === 'paragraph'` (lines 185-193), a document containing the perfectly ordinary CommonMark heading `Heading\n-` now renders as a paragraph plus an empty `
` instead of `

Heading

`. The originating issue only asks that the *nested empty bullet under a list item* stop producing an `

`; it says nothing about single-dash setext headings at top level. The design-doc paragraph added in `docs/design/notes/notes.md` claims the deviation is narrow and that "ordinary setext headings still render", but that is only true for `---`/`=`; single `-` is an equally ordinary and spec-valid setext underline, so existing user notes silently lose headings. The PR's own todo doc lists a "top-level lone dash" test (`docs/tasks/active/20260724-notes-empty-bullet-setext-todo.md:60`) yet no such test appears in `preview.test.ts`, so the intended blast radius was never pinned down.

union.summary: ~60 lines of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule are vendored/forked into the repo rather than wrapped, duplicating third-party code that must be kept in sync
union.evidence: `lheadingRule` is an admitted verbatim copy of upstream `markdown-it 14.x rules_block/lheading.mjs` ("Mirrors the upstream rule ... with a single added guard"), including the token-emission tail, `parentType` juggling, and a hand-re-implemented `asciiTrim` (lines 17-24, "Re-created here so we don't reach into a private markdown-it export"). The same file demonstrates the non-duplicating alternative one function below: `wrappedList` delegates to the original rule via `getRuleFn` and only special-cases the shape it cares about. Forking the rule means every markdown-it upgrade silently keeps the stale 14.3 copy of `lheading` (including any upstream bug fixes to setext parsing) for notes, which is exactly the reuse-over-reimplementation expectation this repo is built around.

union.summary: Plugin reaches into markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry instead of using the supported `ruler.before()` extension point
union.evidence: `getRuleFn` casts `md.block.ruler` to `{ __rules__: Array<{name, fn, enabled}> }` and searches it, with the comment "markdown-it's Ruler exposes no public getter, so we read its private `__rules__` registry". The supported way to add the empty-bullet-interrupts-paragraph behavior is a new rule registered with `md.block.ruler.before('list', 'empty_bullet', fn, { alt: ['paragraph', 'reference', 'blockquote'] })`, which returns `false` for everything it doesn't handle and needs no access to the stock `list` function — and which also removes the `Ruler.at` alt-chain footgun the lessons doc had to record (line 197-201). Choosing private internals here makes the notes preview break on a dependency bump rather than at compile time.

union.summary: Behavior is broadened to `*` and `+` empty bullets, beyond the issue's and the design doc's stated "lone single `-`" scope
union.evidence: `isEmptyBulletLine` accepts `-`, `*` and `+` (`if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a && marker !== 0x2b)`), so `text\n  *` and `text\n  +` now also interrupt a paragraph and produce an empty nested item — a CommonMark deviation the issue never reports (only `-` can be mistaken for a setext underline, which is the entire premise of the bug). The design doc text added at `docs/design/notes/notes.md` frames the deviation as "a **lone single `-`** (the empty-bullet shape)", and no test covers `*`/`+`. Ordered empty markers (`1.`) are also excluded, so the resulting rule set is neither the issue's scope nor a consistent general rule.

union.evidence: The plugin is registered only on the module-level `md` singleton in `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts`. The design doc paragraph references `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-preview.css`, implying at least one frontend-side notes preview surface; if any additional `new MarkdownIt(...)` exists (frontend, server-side rendering, export-to-HTML), it will still render `- 1\n  -` as an `<h2>`, so the user-visible outcome in the issue would only be fixed on one surface. I could not verify because the working tree was not materialized in my environment — no `packages/` or `docs/` directory was reachable — so this needs a `new MarkdownIt(` grep across the repo.

union.summary: The lheading override is global, not scoped to the reported nested-bullet case — it breaks legitimate single-dash setext headings (`Heading\n-`) everywhere in notes
union.evidence: `const isLoneDash = marker === DASH && runLength === 1; if (pos >= max && !isLoneDash) { level = ... }` — the guard fires for ANY paragraph followed by a lone `-`, including a top-level `Heading\n-`, which is a perfectly valid CommonMark setext h2. The issue only reports the *indented, nested-under-a-list-item* case, and both the design-doc paragraph (`docs/design/notes/notes.md`, "deliberately and narrowly") and the todo's plan claim the deviation is narrow. The implementation does not check `state.blkIndent`/list context at all, so the deviation is far broader than the issue asked for and silently removes a supported markdown feature. The plan's own Steps line even lists a `top-level lone dash` test case, which is not present in `preview.test.ts` — the one case that would have exposed this scope is the one left untested.

union.summary: Wholesale copy of markdown-it's upstream `lheading` rule (plus a re-implementation of its private `asciiTrim`) vendored into the repo, rather than reusing/delegating to the existing rule
union.evidence: The file states it "Mirrors the upstream rule (markdown-it 14.x `rules_block/lheading.mjs`) with a single added guard", and lines ~20-27 re-create markdown-it's private `asciiTrim` (`ASCII_TRIM_RE`). ~90 lines of third-party parser code are duplicated for a one-line behavioural delta, with no mechanism (pinned version check, drift test, or comment-linked upstream hash) to detect divergence when markdown-it is upgraded. The same effect is achievable by delegating to the captured original rule (the file already has `getRuleFn` for exactly that with `list`) and rejecting the lone-dash shape before/after calling it. This is a reuse/approach-fit violation for a repo that expects reuse over reinvention.

union.summary: Fix is applied only to the preview render pipeline; if the notes editor pane applies its own markdown styling, the symptom in the issue screenshot may persist there
union.evidence: The plugin is wired only into the `MarkdownIt` instance in `packages/notes/src/view/preview.ts`. The issue's screenshot shows the parent list item rendered with Header-2 styling inline in what appears to be an editing surface. If the notes editor uses a separate markdown highlighter/decorator (e.g. a CodeMirror markdown language or a shared rich-text model), the acceptance outcome "parent list item should retain standard body text styling" would still fail in the editor, and the fix would be incomplete. I could not open the notes package to confirm whether a second markdown-styling path exists.

union.summary: Deviation extends to `*` and `+` empty bullets, which the issue never reports, broadening the CommonMark departure beyond the requested scope
union.evidence: `if (marker !== DASH && marker !== 0x2a /* * */ && marker !== 0x2b /* + */) return false;` — `isEmptyBulletLine` lets an empty `*`/`+` bullet interrupt a paragraph too. Only `-` is implicated by the setext ambiguity in issue #517; `*`/`+` empty bullets are a separate, unrequested CommonMark deviation (`1\n*` etc.), and neither the design-doc paragraph nor the todo's acceptance criteria mention them. No test covers them either.

union.summary: Depends on markdown-it's private `__rules__` registry to fetch the stock `list` rule — a layering/abstraction fit concern
union.evidence: `const ruler = md.block.ruler as unknown as { __rules__: Array<...> }` with the comment "markdown-it's Ruler exposes no public getter, so we read its private `__rules__` registry". Coupling a notes-local plugin to a dependency's private field makes the fix fragile across markdown-it upgrades; the same delegation could be obtained by capturing the rule via a public mechanism (e.g. wrapping at `md.use` time from a known import) or by not replacing `list` at all and instead only relaxing the paragraph terminator path.

union.summary: New `docs/tasks/active/` files added without regenerating the generated tasks index (`docs/tasks/README.md`)
union.evidence: `tasks-index.mjs` generates `docs/tasks/README.md` with an "Active Tasks" table from files matching `^(\d{8})-(.+)-(todo|lessons)\.md$` in `docs/tasks/active/`, and `hooks/post-task-reminder.sh` step 4 tells agents to run `pnpm tasks:archive && pnpm tasks:index`. The diff adds two matching active-task files but contains no corresponding `docs/tasks/README.md` update, leaving the index stale.
